analysis: Examined .github/workflows/release-provider.yml head lines 1–1064 against the indexed threat model and supplied T-041 detail. Visible changes move source resolution (135) and SDK qualification aggregation (304) from Blacksmith Linux to GitHub-hosted ubuntu-24.04, and add a 90-minute signing-job timeout (343). No concrete security regression is established: source verification still precedes credential-consuming jobs (150–189), signing requires successful qualification or validated retained-build recovery (336–340), unsigned inputs remain bound to artifact IDs/digests and source/version (457–479), and final signature, entitlement, archive and full CodeDirectory checks remain intact (767–783, 857–1025). Signing-key removal precedes execution of signed products (718–731); cluster-fact generation remains gated and verifies the retained bundle hash (1039–1055). Relevant contracts are A-005/A-011/A-017 and T-013/T-054; these changes do not visibly alter serving authorization, hop encryption, prompt/cache handling or billing. No evidence establishes weaker isolation or credential exposure on the replacement runners. Integration should examine the later stage-release/publish-release runner changes at head 1211/1320, whose surrounding source is outside these units, and reconcile signing-timeout cleanup with the remaining workflow steps. Referenced script implementations and unchanged callers were not reviewed here; their absence is a coverage limit, not proof of safety or a new vulnerability.
